input.quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
input.rationale: Section 9(b) contains most of the preferred warranty content — performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from material errors (p0038), no malicious code (p0036), compliance with Laws (p0041) — and the Section 13 disclaimer expressly carves out "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language does not swallow the express warranties. However, there is no conformance-to-specification/documentation warranty and no warranty remedy anywhere in the Agreement (no "refund", "re-performance" or "sole remedy" language appears), leaving us without the repair/replace/refund entitlement the playbook requires. We inserted a 90-day conformance warranty plus the standard re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy as new Section 9(b)(xii); the existing warranties run for the Term, which already meets or exceeds the preferred duration.

proposal.summary: Add conformance-to-specification warranty period and repair/replace/refund remedy to Kubient's warranties
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Kubient's warranties in Section 9(b) have no conformance-to-specification commitment and no stated remedy, so we have added a 90-day conformance warranty and the standard re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy. Our position is that the vendor must stand behind its work with a real remedy; we can discuss making the refund the fallback only where re-performance is not practicable.

ops.text: (xii) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Service and each deliverable provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to the applicable specifications and documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 9(b) is, at Kubient's option, prompt re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Service or deliverable.
